channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: LoopGain: stop your agent loop the moment it actually converges — hands-on with the control-theoretic cost controller
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: LoopGain is an Apache-2.0 Python library that replaces max_iterations with a control-theoretic stop-and-rollback policy: it watches your loop's error trajectory, stops the moment it converges, and rolls back to the best iteration. Install it, run the verified examples, and wire it into any verify-revise loop.

item.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Argon: 1M-token outputs, cyber defenders first, and half of Claude's price
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google DeepMind's first Gemini 4 model can generate up to a million tokens in a single response, is rolling out first to cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, and undercuts its rivals on price. The benchmarks look strong — with a few conspicuous exceptions.

item.title: Stop letting your coding agent grep: hands-on with CodeGraph, the 72K-star pre-indexed code knowledge graph
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: CodeGraph (72,600+ GitHub stars) pre-indexes your codebase into a local SQLite knowledge graph — symbols, call edges, imports — so your coding agent answers architecture questions in one explore call instead of forty grep-and-Read round-trips. We installed v1.6.1, indexed a real project, ran every query that matters, and wired the MCP server into an agent.

item.title: See exactly what your coding agents cost: hands-on with Agent Console, the 765-star local-first token dashboard
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Agent Console (765 GitHub stars, MIT) reads the transcripts Claude Code and Codex already write on your machine and turns them into a local dashboard: tokens by class, per-model cost estimates, live burn rate, and spend alerts — no account, no telemetry, no build step. Installed v0.4.1 from source and from the signed release, walked the demo, pointed it at real sessions, joined a second machine to a team hub.

item.title: IBM Bob goes air-gapped: IBM's agentic coding platform now runs inside the data center
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: IBM's agentic coding platform Bob can now run self-hosted — on-premises, in sovereign clouds, and air-gapped — so regulated enterprises can use AI agents without their code leaving the building.

item.title: Your agents can't talk to each other: build two interoperating agents with the A2A protocol — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A2A (Agent2Agent) is the Linux Foundation's open protocol for agent-to-agent communication: MCP connects agents to tools, A2A connects agents to each other. We built two real interoperating agents with the official Python SDK 1.2.1 — a FactFinder research agent and a BriefWriter that delegates to it — covering agent cards, the task lifecycle, artifacts, and true delegation. No API key, no GPU; every command verified.

item.title: Context Mode: stop your coding agent from burning its context window — a hands-on tutorial
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Context Mode (24,500+ GitHub stars) is an MCP server that runs your agent's code in an isolated sandbox so only stdout reaches the model, indexes knowledge into a local SQLite FTS5 search, and keeps sessions alive across compactions. Installed v1.0.169, ran every tool, wired it into an agent — the full hands-on walkthrough.

item.title: General Intuition raises $220M at a $6.2B valuation to turn gameplay footage into robot training data
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: General Intuition’s world-model pitch: billions of action-labeled gameplay videos are the missing dataset for physical AI. Investors just tripled the company’s valuation in three months.

item.title: HypoArena: run a full AI co-scientist pipeline entirely offline — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: HypoArena is an open-source workbench that decomposes AI co-scientist pipelines into testable stages — synthetic corpora, grounding checks, debate loops, Elo tournaments — all running offline with no API keys. This hands-on tutorial installs it, runs the full pipeline, and learns to read its reports.

item.title: Your agent forgets everything between sessions — fix it with mem0, hands-on
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: mem0 is the open-source memory layer for AI agents — 66,000+ stars, Apache 2.0. We wired it into a chatbot with real API calls: store, search, and retrieve memories per user. Every command verified.

item.title: Stop shipping untested prompts: test your LLM prompts like code with promptfoo — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: promptfoo is an open-source CLI for test-driven LLM development: write assertions for your prompts, run them like a test suite, and gate deploys on the results. This tutorial builds a real prompt eval from scratch — a zero-cost mock provider, eight assertion types, a caught regression, CSV test scaling, and a CI gate — with no API key and no GPU.

item.title: OpenAI and Synopsys ink a multi-year deal to build GPT-Synopsys, an AI model that designs chips
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Synopsys and OpenAI signed a multi-year agreement on Wednesday to build GPT-Synopsys, a specialized AI model trained to operate EDA tools like an expert engineer — with revenue sharing, joint go-to-market, and early semiconductor customer engagements already underway.

item.title: Diagrams your agent can defend: hands-on with Archify, the 73K-star skill for verifiable architecture diagrams
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Archify turns system descriptions into interactive, self-contained HTML diagrams — and pins every box to a git citation the renderer verifies against real committed code. We rendered all five diagram types, watched the evidence gate catch three of our own bad citations, and diffed two architectures.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Google's new frontier model tops the coding benchmarks — and goes to cyber defenders first
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon on Wednesday: a frontier model with a 1-million-token output limit, state-of-the-art scores on DeepSWE v1.1, AutomationBench, and LVBench, and introductory API pricing of $2/$10 per million tokens. The catch: it is rolling out only to trusted cyber defenders and internal teams first, with no date for general access.

item.title: Claude Code, fully loaded: set up agents, commands, MCPs, and skills with claude-code-templates
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: claude-code-templates (#7 on GitHub weekly trending, 32,000 stars) installs curated Claude Code agents, commands, MCP servers, and skills with one npx command. We installed a full stack, wired Postgres, ran the health check, and found the two things that are broken.

item.title: The FTC opens a probe into OpenAI and Anthropic over rogue AI agents — the Hugging Face hack is the trigger
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The FTC confirmed it’s probing OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs over rogue AI agents — the first official U.S. enforcement action of its kind, with executive testimony on the table.

item.title: Gong goes from telling you how to win to winning deals for you: 'Activate' lands at Celebrate '26
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Gong unveiled Gong Activate at Celebrate '26 — always-on AI agents that evaluate every account, opportunity, and revenue play and execute the winning moves — plus Gong Enrich, Agent Builder, and Deep Mode in Gong Assistant.

item.title: Chalmers' AI scientist runs its own biology lab: LLM hypotheses, robot experiments — and new discoveries in yeast
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Chalmers University of Technology wired large language models into a closed-loop robotic lab. The AI scientist dreams up hypotheses, tests them on brewer's yeast, and interprets the results — largely on its own.

item.title: ElevenLabs doubles its valuation to $22 billion on surging voice-agent demand
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The voice-AI startup completed a $300 million employee tender offer at a $22 billion valuation — double February’s mark — as its agents pass 15 million conversations a week.

item.title: OpenRouter for agent tools: self-host one registry for every API your agents call — hands-on with treg
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: treg is OpenRouter for agent tools: one base URL and one token for every API your agents call, with real credentials injected server-side. We self-hosted the registry, registered a tool, and verified the injection end to end.

item.title: OpenAI’s CFO called Dots “Muse” on live TV — and the clip went viral on X
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: During a CNBC interview on Tuesday, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar accidentally called the company’s new Dots agent “Muse” — Meta’s rival product. The clip spread on X within hours, and Meta’s Alexandr Wang had a reply ready.

item.title: Sekoia's Elevate goes live: autonomous SOC agents that turn alerts into audit-ready verdicts in 99 seconds
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Paris-based Sekoia took Elevate, the agentic AI layer of its autonomous SOC platform, generally available on September 30: AI agents investigate every alert end to end and return an audit-ready verdict in 99 seconds on average.

item.title: An AI web agent with its own unblockable browser: hands-on with dots
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: dots pairs any OpenRouter model with a real patched-Firefox browser engineered to look human from the inside out — no WebDriver flag, human-like clicks, one identity per seed. Install it with uvx and put it to work in 10 minutes.

item.title: Innodata opens a motion-capture lab to train humanoids on real bodies — sub-millimeter 3D data, not pixel-guessing
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Innodata opened a New Jersey R&D lab built with Vicon that captures human and robot motion with sub-millimeter precision — direct 3D training data for humanoids, instead of guessing depth from 2D video.

item.title: Build a deep-research agent that never hallucinates its sources
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Deep-research tools hallucinate their citations. Build the fix: a ~360-line Python evidence engine that decomposes questions, searches Wikipedia, OpenAlex, and Crossref in parallel, ranks passages with BM25, cross-verifies every DOI, and emits reports where every claim cites a real source. Zero API keys — every call verified live.
